text: Jaffle Shop's leadership is done running analytics like a one-person side project. This capstone starts with their real ask: a governed, production-grade analytics platform, not another ad hoc SQL file.

Paraphrased, the complaint is this: every number comes from somebody's personal SQL file, nobody knows if it's still right, and when something breaks, the business finds out from a confused VP instead of an alert.

That unpacks into five concrete gaps: role-based access control instead of shared passwords, real tests and visible lineage instead of untested SQL, and a scheduled ingestion script plus a CI/CD gate instead of manual loads and unchecked changes.

The next six chapters close those five gaps, one at a time: Snowflake roles and warehouses, then a governed dbt model layer, then tests and documentation as an actual gate, a Python ingestion script, a CI/CD pipeline, and finally Power BI sitting on top of all of it.

This capstone assumes Jaffle Shop's staging models and marts already exist from the earlier tiers — the job here isn't re-teaching ref and select, it's building the governance and production layer around work you can already do. Next: planning the full architecture.
